statements.t: The Company also completed Bitdeer mining machine installations across three sites and advanced engineering and site work for planned superintelligence factories focused on AI inference, including an initial basis-of-design package for a Kentucky project and boundary surveys at two Kentucky development sites.

"We doubled our contracted power capacity to approximately 100 MW, completed Bitdeer installations across three sites and advanced engineering for our planned superintelligence factories, including an initial basis-of-design package for a Kentucky project and boundary surveys at two of our Kentucky development sites.
Power, land and local support are what determine whether a project actually gets built, and we are building trust site by site rather than assuming it will just be there."
The Company plans to use modular builds at suitable existing industrial sites, including locations with power infrastructure already in place.
On September 30, 2026, a subsidiary of the Company signed a 50 MW Data Center Project Power Contract with Hopkinsville Electric System in Kentucky.
The Company intends to use these funds for working capital and general corporate purposes, including AI and HPC development in the TVA region.
In October 2026, the Company's engineering and modular infrastructure partners prepared preliminary layouts for three projects in Kentucky and Tennessee.

While we are undergoing the transformation of our existing sites to HPC and AI workloads, we will continue to provide hosting services to third parties, including a 30 MW arrangement with Bitdeer across three sites in Tennessee and Kentucky, which we expect to provide more predictable revenue.
We believe the next phase of AI growth will be increasingly driven by AI inference, which we expect to favor a broader footprint of smaller sites that can be developed and deployed more rapidly.

As AI adoption moves beyond the training of models into everyday software and business use, we anticipate a growing share of computing demand to come from the inference of the ongoing processing of AI workloads in production.

Our energized power positions, located primarily in the Tennessee Valley Authority region, may facilitate faster and a more capital efficient path to deployment relative to projects that have not yet secured interconnection or require additional infrastructure development.
We intend to differentiate through execution, site readiness and community engagement, and to replicate this approach across our growing portfolio.
We do not currently plan to hold Bitcoin and we regularly convert Bitcoin received for services into U.S. dollars.
In October 2026, our engineering and modular infrastructure partners prepared preliminary layouts for three projects in Kentucky and Tennessee.
We intend to carry the engineering work, supplier coordination and utility relationships from these projects into a repeatable development program.
On September 30, 2026, one of our subsidiaries entered into a 50 MW Data Center Project Power Contract with Hopkinsville Electric System, doubling our contracted capacity to 100 MW.
Pursuant to the terms of the agreement, we will guarantee up to a maximum aggregate liability of $10.0 million, in connection with the proposed new data center in Hopkinsville, Kentucky.
We expect to continue to expand our revenue mix and utilization for the remainder of 2026.
We expect to fund our operations going forward with existing cash resources, revenue from our operations, and cash that we may raise through future financing transactions.
We intend to use the net proceeds from the Private Placement for working capital and general corporate purposes, including funding our AI and HPC development in the Tennessee Valley Authority region.
If all of the warrants are exercised for cash, we would expect to receive additional gross proceeds of approximately $5.8 million.
We expect that any proceeds received from the facility will be used primarily for working capital and general corporate purposes and in furtherance of our corporate strategy.

Management has projected that based on our recurring losses and negative cash flows from operating activities, cash on hand may not be sufficient to allow us to continue operations and there is substantial doubt about our ability to continue as a going concern within 12 months from the date of issuance of our financial statements if we are unable to raise additional funding for operations.
We expect our working capital needs to increase in the future as we continue to expand and enhance our operations.
To mitigate these risks, we expect that recently contracted hosting agreements should further support these efforts.

Significant changes from our current forecasts, including but not limited to: (i) shortfalls from projected earnings; (ii) increases in operating costs; (iii) decreases in the value of cryptocurrency; and (iv) if we do not maintain compliance with the requirements of Nasdaq and/or we do not maintain our listing with Nasdaq, it could have a material adverse impact on our ability to access the level of funding…
Management believes the CBP allegation of Chinese origin on the imported miners to be without merit and intend to defend against these claims vigorously.
We will continue to evaluate the likelihood of achieving the milestone and assess any resulting impact on liquidity, capital resources, and future cash flows.

As of September 30, 2026, the proposal has not yet received all requisite regulatory approvals which could affect the project’s feasibility, timing, or scope, as such we are not committed to the offered estimated cost at this time.

On September 30, 2026, one of our subsidiaries entered into a 50 MW Data Center Project Power Contract with HES, pursuant to which we will guarantee the payment and performance of all of our subsidiary’s obligations under the contract, up to a maximum aggregate liability of $10.0 million.
